name: media-frame
title: Media frame
description: The space a piece of the host's media occupies, and nothing else. It is not a video player and must never become one: the video, the 3D scene, the canvas and the embed belong to the host, exactly as a stage's scene does, and the frame renders whatever it is passed without loading, decoding, buffering, playing, pausing, seeking or timing any of it. What it does own is the space. It holds an aspect ratio and a floor height, so a frame whose source has not arrived is the same size as one that worked and nothing under it jumps when the media lands. A frame with nothing in it is a designed empty state carrying `data-gs-empty`, naming what belongs there and the shape it is holding, never a blank rectangle; a frame the host has declared `data-gs-busy` still shows that content, which is what the attribute contract requires. `data-gs-playing` is the host's word repeated, on the same footing as busy: the host declares it and the library never infers it, because the frame never touches the media.
docs: Pass `label`, which is what belongs in the frame in your own words: "portrait video", "the qualifying replay". It is required rather than defaulted, because a frame that cannot say what it is waiting for is the blank rectangle this component exists to prevent, and it is the frame's accessible name.
